title.en: The hundredth tiger and the wooden toy

hook.en: The king has killed ninety-nine tigers. The hundredth one turns out to be the most dangerous of all, and it is made of wood.

objectives.en: Narrate the hunt for the hundredth tiger

narration.en: The king has killed ninety-nine tigers. The hundredth one turns out to be the most dangerous of all, and it is made of wood.

body.en: Unable to find a hundredth tiger, the king grows desperate and the frightened Dewan arranges one: an old tiger brought from the People's Park in Madras and set loose near a village. The king shoots and misses, but believes he has killed it. The tiger, only fainted from shock, is quietly killed by the hunters so the king never learns the truth.

say.en: The Dewan brings an old tiger from a park in Madras.
The king misses; the hunters kill it secretly.
He buys a wooden toy tiger for his son.
A sliver of wood pricks his hand.
The infection spreads, and the king dies.

body.en: For his son's third birthday the king buys a wooden toy tiger, crudely carved and wildly overpriced. While he plays with it, a sliver of wood pricks his right hand. The wound becomes infected, he needs surgery, and he dies. The hundredth tiger has taken its revenge, and the prophecy comes true.

problem.en: How is the ending of "The Tiger King" an example of irony?

steps.en: The king killed real tigers to save his life.
He believes he has killed the hundredth, but he has not.
A harmless toy tiger finally causes his death.
So the prophecy comes true in an unexpected way.

answer.en: The king slaughters ninety-nine real tigers and believes he has killed the hundredth, yet his bullet had missed. The fatal blow comes from a cheap wooden toy tiger bought for his son, whose sliver causes a deadly infection. The mighty hunter is defeated by a plaything, and the prophecy is fulfilled.
